system.one_liner: Synthetic-to-real pose adaptation that adds a reconstruction loss from bone-map warping of a base image to a driving image, on top of integrated pseudo-labels.

content.variant_note: panel (a) wires the fine-tuning modules on a real image pair, panel (b) opens the warping estimation module as a formula chain with intermediate maps
content.argues: Reconstructing the driving image from the base image through keypoint-derived bone-map warping supplies an extra supervisory signal that complements pseudo-labels for fine-tuning on unlabelled target data.
content.subject: Keypoint predictor, pseudo-labelling P, warping estimation W and generator G on a base and driving image pair, with W opened in a second panel.

evidence: The geometric reconstruction consists of Warping Estimation Module W and Generation Module G, as shown in Fig. 1(a).
With the transformation and base images, a hourglass is used to generate inpainting map Cdrv←b and region-wise displacement ﬁeld Ddrv←b

summary: The paper adapts pose estimators from synthetic to real data without labels, adding image reconstruction to pseudo-labelling. Figure 1(a) shows a base and a driving photo of a person entering a keypoint predictor f_enc and f_dec. Heatmaps and depth go to the orange pseudo-labelling block P and the grey warping estimation module W, whose inpainting map and displacement field drive the generator G, which redraws the driving photo. A dashed key defines the symbols. Panel (b) opens W: heatmaps, keypoints, bone maps, SVD and Expand, a deformation of the base image and an hourglass that outputs the two maps. Thumbnails sit at the inputs and outputs; the style is flat vector with serif math.
